written.myAnswer: Calcium reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to form calcium sulphate and hydrogen: Ca + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ + H₂. The sparingly soluble CaSO₄ may form a coating on the calcium.
NaHCO₃ behaves as a base because it reacts with an acid to form a salt, water and carbon dioxide.
2NH₄Cl + H₂SO₄ → (NH₄)₂SO₄ + 2HCl; 2NH₄NO₃ + H₂SO₄ → (NH₄)₂SO₄ + 2HNO₃; MgO + H₂SO₄ → MgSO₄ + H₂O; MgCO₃ + H₂SO₄ → MgSO₄ + H₂O + CO₂.
A base reacts with a non-metallic oxide to form salt and water. This shows that non-metallic oxides are acidic in nature.
(i) For a short duration, lime water turns milky because insoluble CaCO₃ forms. (ii) With excess CO₂, the milkiness disappears as soluble Ca(HCO₃)₂ forms.
